title: LHCb observes CP violation for the first time in baryon decays
summary: Using 9 fb⁻¹ of LHCb Run 1 and Run 2 data, the collaboration measured a phase-space-averaged CP asymmetry of (2.45 ± 0.46 ± 0.10)% in Λb⁰ → pK⁻π⁺π⁻ and its conjugate, a 5.2σ observation. In the resonance-dominated R(pπ⁺π⁻)K⁻ region, the asymmetry was (5.4 ± 0.9 ± 0.1)%, 6.0σ from zero. Machine-learning BDT selection suppressed combinatorial background; neural-network PID variables mitigated particle misidentification.
ai_technology: Boosted decision tree event classifier; neural-network particle-identification variables

evidence.tested: Using 9 fb⁻¹ of LHCb Run 1 and Run 2 data, the collaboration measured a phase-space-averaged CP asymmetry of (2.45 ± 0.46 ± 0.10)% in Λb⁰ → pK⁻π⁺π⁻ and its conjugate, a 5.2σ observation.
evidence.unknown: This is the first reported baryon-decay CP-violation observation, with significance 5.2σ for the phase-space-integrated result and 6.0σ in the specified resonance region. Reported asymmetries average over phase space; the paper says a full amplitude-structure investigation remains future work. Small asymmetries may cancel across angular-momentum amplitudes. The measured CP asymmetry is distinct from raw yield asymmetry; production/detection nuisance asymmetries are subtracted using a control channel.
evidence.ai_role: The BDT used decay topology, displacement and kinematics to suppress random combinations in the four-track signal selection. Neural-network PID variables helped mitigate misidentified final-state particle backgrounds. These tools supported signal purity for the baryon–antibaryon asymmetry measurement.
